g.text: 3 issue(s) found (1 breaking change, 1 security, 1 regression); 2 verified by AST analysis or sandbox execution, 2
candidate(s) filtered by the critic. Most severe: SQL injection: query built from interpolated values at db.py:44.
Blast radius: 6 modified symbol(s), 3 upstream caller(s) within 2 hops.
`db.get_user_transactions` builds a SQL statement with f-string interpolation and passes it to the database driver.
Any caller-controlled value (`limit`, `status`, `user_id`) can terminate the literal and inject SQL (e.g.
`status="x' OR '1'='1"` returns every user's transactions). This violates ADR-001 / OWASP A03.
• [diff] db.py:44: "SELECT id, amount_cents, status, created_at FROM transactions " f"WHERE user_id = {user_id}"
• [static] tainted SQL fragment at db.py:44: "SELECT id, amount_cents, status, created_at FROM transactions "
• [static] tainted SQL fragment at db.py:47: f" AND status = '{status}'"
• [static] tainted SQL fragment at db.py:48: f" ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT {limit}"
• [static] query string flows into a DB-API execute() call in the same function
• [policy] [builtin:owasp-a03] OWASP A03:2021 Injection / CWE-89 SQL Injection
Suggested fix: Use DB-API placeholders and pass values separately, e.g. `conn.execute("... WHERE user_id = ? AND
status = ? LIMIT ?", (user_id, status, limit))`; append optional clauses as fixed strings and collect parameters in
`api_routes.get_current_user` calls `verify_token(_bearer(authorization), AUTH_SECRET)`, but the PR changes
`verify_token(token: str, secret: str)` → `verify_token(token: str, secret: str, audience: str)` (new required
parameter `audience`). At runtime this raises `TypeError` (missing required argument `audience`). Blast radius:
• [static] AST contract check: missing required argument `audience`
• [diff] auth.py:47: verify_token(token: str, secret: str, audience: str)
Suggested fix: Update the call site to satisfy the new signature, or keep `verify_token` backward compatible by
A synthesized pytest run against both revisions shows `payments.calculate_split_fee` now crashes where the base
revision did not: `participants=0` → ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero; `participants=<omitted>`
→ TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for //: 'int' and 'NoneType'. Callers passing these values get an unhandled
exception instead of a validation error.
